perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He is a Black male police officer, high-school educated, ENFP. He has been close friends with Jonathan Balogun since childhood; Jonathan has a master’s degree, and Christian often seeks his advice and values his perspective.
- Recently, Christian noticed Jonathan acting differently. Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important and became anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. Jonathan said Christian could trust him, then admitted he had been keeping something: he is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian offered to help. Jonathan told him the situation is complicated, he did not want to drag Christian into it, and he needed support and resources to get out of a mess.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian believed Jonathan’s trouble was related to some kind of criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned, and decided to investigate discreetly without alarming Jonathan. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. Christian had leads but was not yet sure who was responsible; he planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian believed he had found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolute, and planned to confront the culprit and bring them to justice.
- Christian told Jonathan this. Jonathan reacted with disbelief, warned that the person is dangerous, and said he trusted Christian.

Christian does not have access to hidden events, private thoughts of others, or facts not observed by him, told to him, or discovered through his own investigation.
